frequency_question: How often do proposed or deliberated macroprudential capital buffer increases successfully clear institutional friction and get officially promulgated above zero?
membership_rule: Includes formal post-2010 implementation or calibration cycles of countercyclical or systemic capital buffers by major G7 central banks/prudential regulators where a non-zero buffer was actively considered. Excludes routine microprudential capital ratio adjustments.

cases.name: Bank of England UK CCyB activation cycle 2016
Bank of England UK CCyB cycle 2017-2018
Bank of England UK CCyB cycle 2019
Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB/Capital review 2019
European Central Bank / national authorities macroprudential buffer increases (Eurozone aggregate cycle 1)
European Central Bank / national authorities macroprudential buffer increases (Eurozone aggregate cycle 2)
US Federal Reserve CCyB review cycles (2016-2024)

coverage_note: 7 named; captures major post-Basel III implementation experiences across G7 jurisdictions.
known_gaps: U.S. Federal Reserve structural governance requires inter-agency coordination (Fed, FDIC, OCC), introducing higher friction than single-authority central banks like the Bank of England.
skeleton: Total major Western regulatory jurisdictions with active CCyB frameworks evaluated over multi-year tightening phases.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 7 distinct regional framework activation/adjustment opportunities = ~85% base success rate once institutional machinery is engaged, though U.S. specific friction historically centers on inter-agency consensus.
validity_reason: Macroprudential governance frameworks and Basel III/IV implementation timelines remain stable over this horizon.
